title: finding(tests): both find-absence controls in ListView.objectProviderBinding-7477 stay green against a query started 50ms after mount
body:
Filed as an out-of-scope by-product of objectui#8703 (branch `claude/issue-8703-matcher-dependent-strict-bucket`). Not claimed, not assigned. objectui#8703 recorded this as an explicitly **unmeasured** observation and left it to its reader to measure or to leave declared. It was measured. It reproduces.

## The pins

`packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.objectProviderBinding-7477.test.tsx`

- line 205 — `invents NO binding from an 'object' provider that names no object`: `expect(dataSource.find).not.toHaveBeenCalled();`
- line 218 — `leaves the 'value' provider alone — it never gains an objectName`: the same assertion.

Both are read straight after `await waitFor(() => expect(kanbanProps.length).toBeGreaterThan(0))`. For an inline-items provider `ListView` starts with `loading === false`, so those props arrive on the FIRST commit and the absence is dated to mount, not to a settled load.

## Forced

An implementation strictly worse than the bug: one line in `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`, right after `const dataSource = props.dataSource;`, that starts a query 50ms after mount on every path.

```
React.useEffect(() => { setTimeout(() => {
  (dataSource as any)?.find?.('__ablation_probe__', {});
}, 50); }, []);
```

Mutation proven on disk both directions (`git hash-object` vs the HEAD blob, anchor counts, line-total gate) and restored by state (`git diff HEAD` empty).

**Leg 1 — with the probe: 7 of 7 tests pass.** Both `not.toHaveBeenCalled()` pins stay green while a query is being issued 50ms after every mount.

**Leg 2 — is the deferred query actually landing inside the control test?** A temporary diagnostic appended to the `value`-provider test, after its existing pin:

```
await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 300));
expect(dataSource.find).toHaveBeenCalled();
```

With the probe: **7 of 7 pass** — so within that one test, `find` was un-called at pin time and called 300ms later, on the same mock.

**Leg 3 — the control that makes leg 2 mean something.** The identical test mutation (same blob, `9b245eda9bde4e8921531a66ea84ca61c6665ab1`) with `ListView.tsx` pristine (`ef7cf802d719944519bb11d1891904c14b5cb078`, equal to its HEAD blob): the diagnostic **fails** — `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called at least once`, 6 passed / 1 failed. So `find` is not otherwise called, and the diagnostic can fail.

Per-test classification from vitest's JSON reporter in all three legs; zero death strings.

## What this does and does not say

- It does **not** say `ListView` has a bug today. Nothing in the current implementation defers a query on these paths.
- It says the two pins cannot distinguish "starts no query" from "starts a query a tick later", which is the regression shape that would otherwise reach them. An implementation strictly worse than the bug passes them.
- It is **outside** the objectui#8690 / objectui#8703 detector's population: a mock-call absence, not a recorder array. No census flag points here.

A repair is a settle window before the absence is read — the same move objectui#8664 and objectui#8690 made on the recorder sites — and it needs its own forced leg, because an absence pin that never fails has not been tested.

## Dedup — declared

`search_issues` returns false zeros in this repo, so a zero would not be evidence. The query run here was not a zero: `ListView value provider control asserts find not called, deferred query after mount would pass, pin is vacuous` scoped to this repo returned two hits (objectui#7947, objectui#4567) — a self-validating non-empty result, neither of them this.
